text:
Elaine: hey @eng-runtime — quick ask for our webinar next Tues. We need a reproducibility + provenance package for the launch benchmark claims. Can you confirm feasibility by EOD Fri?

Mateo: sgtm, can you enumerate exact artifact locations / format expectations?

Elaine: ideally a single tar.gz with: payloads/{cohorts}, seeds.txt, run_configs.json, warmup_logs/, latency_percentiles.csv, raw_token_counts.csv, run_manifest.txt with git sha and run-id. Also a small README.md describing sampling methodology and any postprocessing. compress with gzip.

Jin: we can do that. couple q's: which models / quant variants need to be included? do you need coldstart traces or just steady-state? what's acceptable for missing samples?

Elaine: Primary models: open-llama-13b, rw-7b-quant, rw-1-compat (fallback). include quant variants only if they materially change latency. we want a coldstart heatmap for the demo but not full per-request traces. missing samples: <1% permissible but flag them.

Mateo: ok — we'll produce run_manifest with fields: run_id, git_sha, model, batch_size, seq_len, quant, kernel_version. we'll also include provenance mapping file (input_id -> original_payload_bucket_path).

Raj: also include prompt templates and any postprocessing scripts (detokenize / normalization) — otherwise outputs won't match. pinging artifact-bot to upload once ready.

artifact-bot: Artifact Uploader: created upload ticket ART-2025-881. Drop tar.gz to s3://redwood-internal/bench-artifacts/ART-2025-881/ and the pipeline will validate checksums.

Mateo: quick helper — to export a run we use:```
./scripts/export_run.sh --run-id $RUN_ID --out /tmp/run.tar.gz
```this will collect logs + configs + traces.

Jin: ETA: we can assemble on Thu and run a quick verification Fri morning. will marketing need a signed note about warmup behavior (e.g., sessions used for cache warmup)?

Elaine: yes, a brief paragraph about warmup protocol and any observed variance. also want 50/90/95 percentiles for latency and a small cost-per-token summary.

Mateo: noted. one more ask: can marketing share the exact claim wording we'll put in the deck so we can annotate numbers appropriately?

Elaine: current draft: 'Redwood reduces per-token inference cost by up to 3x and maintains 95th percentile latency under 120ms on common workloads.' don't be picky yet — we'll iterate. please annotate any numbers that are best-case vs representative.

Jin: we'll add annotations in README for best-case vs typical, and flag any warmup-only numbers. putting placeholder run-id ART-2025-881 in docs now.

Elaine: :thumbsup: thanks team. if anything blocks ping me. i'll open a tiny marketing ticket with the draft claims and link the ART-2025-881 upload path so we can cross-check after the verification run. cc Raj for eval notes.
